transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Falcon Head of Partnerships), Carlos Mendez (Falcon Channel Sales), Ava Brooks (Falcon Solutions Architect)

Summary/Notes (auto): quick pipeline review focused on 3 co-sell opps, technical clarifications on private deployment, next step to schedule exec briefing and share GTM materials.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. We'll go through the joint pipeline, quick status updates, and surface any blockers. Liam's here for technical questions.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya, appreciate it. Morning/afternoon all. We've got Carlos and Ava from my team.
[00:25] Carlos Mendez: Hi all.
[00:27] Ava Brooks: Hello.
[00:30] Liam Ortiz: quick hi from my side, I have notes on VPC and KMS.

[02:00] Maya Chen: Great. High-level — three joint deals: RetailBot Pilot (north star, good fit for co-sell), Healthcare POC (data residency concerns), and FinOps proof (internal buy-in slower). We'll go one by one. Priya, do you want to start with RetailBot pipeline status?
[02:18] Priya Nair: Sure. RetailBot's been engaged three weeks, product team likes Redwood demos, they're asking about dedicated capacity and latency. Sales lead expects procurement to move quickly if we can show a pilot with predictable SLAs. Our channel rep flagged budget is there but they want an exec-level conversation.
[03:05] Maya Chen: That tracks. We recommend Dedicated for a pilot to meet their SLA ask — reserved capacity gives predictable throughput. Liam, any quick notes on latency numbers we can share?
[03:20] Liam Ortiz: For RetailBot with a 2k token context, on a p3-like GPU with our runtime tuned, 95th percentile latency is ~220–280ms, depending on batching. If they need multi-region low-latency we can route by region but costs go up. Note: numbers are approximations; we should run a short benchmark against their sample prompts.
[03:48] Ava Brooks: micro interruption — what about KV cache impacts? Retail has lots of repeated prompts, cache would help right?
[03:54] Liam Ortiz: Yeah, prefix/KV caching reduces tokens per request, saves cost and reduces latency in practice. We'll want representative prompts to tune batch sizes and caching policies.

[05:10] Carlos Mendez: On the exec conversation, Falcon can co-host a briefing with the customer's SVP of commerce — that tends to accelerate procurement. Would Redwood be open to a joint exec deck?
[05:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll put together a short exec-facing slide deck + a proposed pilot timeline and SLOs. We'll also include pricing guidance for a reserved pilot.

[06:00] Priya Nair: Quick Q on security: RetailBot wants assurance around SOC 2, SAML SSO, and encryption keys. Also they'd prefer we keep data in their region. Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS and VPC private deployment?
[06:18] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC deployments and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For hosted we have SOC 2 plus encryption at rest, but for the regulator-sensitive stuff we typically recommend Private. Liam can walk through the integration constraints.
[06:40] Liam Ortiz: For VPC-on-prem or VPC deployments, network peering and private endpoints are straightforward; the main work is routing, egress controls, and provisioning the service account and KMS key. We have an onboarding checklist and a runbook — I'll send a trimmed runbook for Falcon and the joint pilot. There can be some latency overhead depending on network topology.

[08:05] Priya Nair: Perfect, that helps. Can you add the runbook to the shared drive?
[08:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll add it. (link in chat) slides: https://redwood.app/sales/decks/co-sell-retailbot-briefing.pdf

[09:00] Maya Chen: Switching to Healthcare POC — this one has strong interest but data residency and compliance are bigger blockers. Priya, where are we here?
[09:12] Priya Nair: They're leaning to Private deployment or completely on-prem. They're asking for SOC 2 + HIPAA attestation. Also legal wants audit logs for every inference.
[09:30] Maya Chen: Redwood can support audit logs and private deployments; HIPAA workflows need a BAA and some additional controls. We should loop in security/legal. Carlos, do you own the legal handoff?
[09:42] Carlos Mendez: I'll connect legal, yes. We should get Redwood's security pack and BAA template.
[09:50] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC 2 report, BAA draft, and an architecture diagram for on-prem. Liam, any technical nuance?
[10:05] Liam Ortiz: On-prem packaging can be heavier — depends on hardware. If they want an air-gapped install we need to scope images, and quantization/compilation for their GPUs. That will take some lead time, maybe 4–8 weeks depending on procurement.

[12:20] Ava Brooks: Is there a lightweight approach? Like hybrid where model runs in customer region but control plane is Redwood?
[12:30] Liam Ortiz: Hybrid is possible — private control plane + model runtime in their cloud. That usually balances speed-to-value with compliance. We'll outline options in the runbook.

[14:00] Maya Chen: Last deal: FinOps proof — internal champion has been slow, timeline slipped to Q4. Not priority for co-sell this quarter. Any objections?
[14:12] Priya Nair: Agreed, deprioritize for now. Focus on RetailBot and Healthcare.

[15:00] Maya Chen: Pricing/discounting — Carlos, what discount bands are you able to offer for reserved pilots?
[15:08] Carlos Mendez: Falcon's margin allowances are flexible but we prefer standard tiers. For co-sell we can attach an initial promotional discount; we need Redwood's guidance to finalize.
[15:20] Maya Chen: We'll share recommended pricing tiers: one for hosted pilot, one for dedicated reserved capacity. We'll include an example cost estimate for the RetailBot pilot with assumed token counts.

[16:10] Priya Nair: On Go-to-market, Falcon can run a 2-week outreach to top accounts once we have the joint case studies. We need one success story or at least a referenced pilot to start targeted outreach.
[16:25] Maya Chen: Understood. Plan: run the pilot, collect metrics (latency, cost per session, MRR impact), then Falcon will go-to-market. We'll define success metrics now — e.g., 95th percentile latency <300ms, cost per chat drop by 40% vs current, and pilot conversion to a paid contract within 90 days.

[17:40] Ava Brooks: Technical quick question — model variants. RetailBot asked about using a smaller quantized model for transactions and larger model for contextualisation. How does Redwood handle model routing?
[17:52] Liam Ortiz: We support smart routing and model variants. Routing policy can send low-cost requests to quantized variants and overflow or context-heavy ones to higher-quality variants. We can configure fallback when capacity is constrained.

[19:10] Carlos Mendez: Competitors — customer mentioned they're also talking to Anthropic and Bedrock for managed endpoints. Any differentiators we should highlight?
[19:22] Maya Chen: Emphasize unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, explicit cost controls (batching, KV caching), and our GTM partnership support — we co-sell and provide joint materials and executive engagement. Also our ability to run targeted benchmarks with their prompts.

[20:15] Priya Nair: Question: how quickly can Redwood run a benchmark with our sample prompt set and give an actual cost/latency figure?
[20:25] Liam Ortiz: We can run a 48-hour benchmark — end-to-end we can turn something around in 3–5 business days if we have prompts and representative traffic.

[21:05] Maya Chen: Good. So immediate asks: Falcon to share sample prompts + expected concurrency, Redwood to run benchmark and share numbers and a pilot proposal, then schedule the exec briefing.

[22:00] Priya Nair: On exec briefing — suggested attendees: our SVP of Commerce, Redwood AE, Redwood SE, and the customer's SVP. Would Redwood prepare a 20-min tech + 10-min exec summary?
[22:15] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll prepare a concise deck and a proposed timeline. We'll also include the runbook and security pack.

[23:40] Carlos Mendez: Legal question: for the Healthcare POC we need BAA draft and an NDA in place before we share sample PHI prompts.
[23:50] Maya Chen: We'll get legal involved. We'll push BAA and SOC 2 artifacts; please route legal contact to Maya and our legal team email.

[25:00] Priya Nair: Any other technical risks? Ava?
[25:06] Ava Brooks: Mostly around network egress and KMS permissions. We'll validate with our cloud security team. If you can provide detailed steps, we can estimate lead times.

[26:10] Liam Ortiz: I'll include a step-by-step for KMS key sharing and the minimal IAM roles required. Also note that we prefer Customer-Managed KMS for Private deployment for auditability.

[28:00] Maya Chen: Ok pulling together next steps recap. Action items: Maya send deck + pricing guidance; Liam send runbook and KMS steps; Priya confirm exec briefing attendees & dates; Carlos share top account list. We'll aim to run the benchmark once prompts are received.

[29:12] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Any timeline concerns?
[29:20] Maya Chen: If we get prompts this week, benchmark results and pilot proposal by next Friday, then pilot kickoff in early September is achievable.

[30:05] Carlos Mendez: For co-sell attribution — how do we track leads and credit? We want clear rules for referrals and commission splits.

[30:20] Maya Chen: We'll document co-sell attribution in the GTM plan: referral source, person of record, and closed-won split. We'll add an appendix with sample commission tables.

[31:15] Priya Nair: Anything else from the Falcon side?
[31:20] Ava Brooks: Not from me. We'll validate hardware for Healthcare POC and share specs.

[31:40] Maya Chen: Great. We'll also include a short FAQ for sales reps to use in early outreach.

[33:00] Carlos Mendez: One more note — Falcon plans a partner summit in October; if RetailBot pilot is underway by then, we can present a joint session. That could be a strong accelerant.

[33:12] Maya Chen: Perfect — we'll prioritize RetailBot to enable that narrative.

[34:00] Priya Nair: ok, last minute ask — can Redwood provide a short customer reference or a one-pager about a similar retail deployment?
[34:10] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a retail case study and a 1-pager. I'll attach in the follow-up.

[35:05] Liam Ortiz: I'll flag any hard constraints in the runbook that could block an early pilot.

[36:00] Maya Chen: Alright, unless there are other items, let's recap next steps and owners.

[36:10] Priya Nair: Nope, all good. Thanks everyone.

[36:30] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the deck, runbook, and schedule for the exec briefing. Chat links: co-sell slides and runbook will be uploaded to the shared folder.

[36:48] Carlos Mendez: Thanks.

[36:50] Ava Brooks: Thank you.

[36:52] Maya Chen: End.

Auto transcribe notes: transcription may omit overlapping speech and occasional noise.
